You are investigating the Go codebase "memos" at /bench/repo (commit 2d01420). Answer precisely with file:line citations. Read actual code, don't guess. Use grep extensively.

h08 (collision): More than one type declares a method named RunOnce. List every declarer (type — file), and state which declarations are invoked from production (non-test) code, with the caller (path:line). Grep for "func.*RunOnce" and "RunOnce(" call sites. Format: one per line "declarer — invoked? — caller(path)"

h09 (collision): How many distinct declarations of a method named Close exist across the backend (Go files)? Grep "func.*) Close(". List each declarer type and file. Then determine which types' Close is actually called by non-test server code, cite callers. Format: "count; invoked declarers with caller paths"

h10 (aggregation): Which single function or method declared under internal/ has the highest inbound-call count (fan-in), and roughly how many callers? Consider heavily-used utility functions in internal/util/, internal/base/, etc. Use grep to count call sites for candidate functions. Give your best determination. Format: "symbol — path — approx fan-in"

h11 (aggregation): Of the persistent entity types defined in the data layer (store package — e.g. Memo, User, Attachment/Resource, Reaction, Activity, Webhook, IdentityProvider, Inbox, etc.), which one is referenced from the largest number of packages OUTSIDE the store layer? Rank the top two with rough package counts. Grep for "store.Memo", "store.User", etc. across server/, internal/, and count distinct packages. Format: "1st: Type; 2nd: Type (with rough package counts)"

r02 (reality-check): FALSE PREMISE. "Where is the per-user API rate-limiting middleware registered, and what are its request limits?" Determine whether per-user rate-limiting middleware exists at all. Check server/router/ interceptors/middleware. Report premise correction. Format: "premise correction"

Give concrete file:line citations. Report in a numbered list h08, h09, h10, h11, r02.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
All investigations complete. Here are the findings:

## h08 — Method `RunOnce` collision

Two types declare `RunOnce`, both named `Runner` (different packages):

```
*s3presign.Runner  — invoked?  YES  — server/server.go:163 (and self-invoked in Run loop at server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36)
*memopayload.Runner — invoked? NO   — no production caller (only memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload, a standalone func, is used at memo_service.go:108 & :447; the Runner.RunOnce method is dead code)
```

Declarers: `s3presign.Runner` — server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43; `memopayload.Runner` — server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27.

## h09 — Method `Close` declarations

**Count: 6 distinct declarations.**

- `*SSEHub` — server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99
- `*Store` — store/store.go:72
- `*Cache` — store/cache/cache.go:187
- `*DB` (sqlite) — store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67
- `*DB` (postgres) — store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46
- `*DB` (mysql) — store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47

Invoked by non-test server code:
- `Store.Close` — server/server.go:146 (`s.Store.Close()`)
- `SSEHub.Close` — server/server.go:206 (`s.sseHub.Close()`)
- `Cache.Close` — store/store.go:74-76 (`instanceSettingCache/userCache/userSettingCache.Close()`)
- `DB.Close` (sqlite/postgres/mysql) — store/store.go:78 (`s.driver.Close()`, dispatches to the active driver)

## h10 — Highest fan-in symbol under `internal/`

```
util.GenUUID — internal/util/util.go:40 — approx fan-in ~7
```

7 non-test call sites: server/auth/token.go:194, server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go:26 & :135, attachment_service_storage.go:209, shortcut_service.go:154, user_service_access_tokens.go:84, sso_username.go:15. (Nearest competitors: `filter.DefaultEngine` ~7 but mostly internal to the filter package; `util.ConvertStringToInt32` 5; `filter.AppendConditions` 6.)

## h11 — Most-referenced store entity type (outside store package)

```
1st: User (~5-6 packages); 2nd: Memo (~4 packages)
```

- `store.User` — 5 non-test packages: server/auth, server/notification, server/router/api/v1, server/router/fileserver, server/router/rss (6 including server/router/api/v1/test).
- `store.Memo` — 4 packages: server/notification, server/router/api/v1, server/router/rss, server/runner/memopayload.

(Others trail: Attachment 3, Inbox 2; Reaction/Activity/Webhook/IdentityProvider ~0-1.)

## r02 — Premise correction

**Premise is FALSE. No per-user (nor any) API rate-limiting middleware exists in this codebase.** The Connect RPC interceptor chain in server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go registers exactly four interceptors: `MetadataInterceptor` (:22), `LoggingInterceptor` (:98), `RecoveryInterceptor` (:165), and `AuthInterceptor` (:208) — none perform rate limiting. A repo-wide search for rate-limiting constructs (`ratelimit`, `limiter`, `throttle`, `golang.org/x/time/rate`, `tollbooth`) across server/ and internal/ returns only a documentation comment (internal/email/doc.go:86) suggesting email rate-limiting as a future idea — no implementation, no request limits, no registration point.
